journey.quote: 28 years ago, I joined Dr. Jay Crosson in forming the Federation, and I oversaw initially that venture work, new products and services across all of the regions and geographies.

journey.fortune_basis: we could tap into all of them in order to define strategy
journey.quote: 11 years ago, um, we transformed the federation that the core leadership of the federation came from the Permanente Medical groups.

journey.label: Rob Shriner's caution about loving KP
journey.fortune_basis: remember that you can love an organization, but an organization can never love you back.
journey.quote: Rob Shriner, um, who is the Medical Director in Georgia, he, he he once said to me, Chris, you care too much about Kaiser Permanente.

journey.quote: having been part of Kaiser Permanente for over three decades, um, I've seen I've been on the ground in every geography I've seen us, you know, geographically expand and then contract.

retellable.title: The NICU nurse at two a.m.
retellable.summary: Less than a year into his job, after working until 2 a.m. on the EMR business case, Grant stopped at the Geary Street NICU and found a nurse rocking, feeding and singing to his premature son. He told his wife that night he had found his calling.
retellable.quote: as I leaned closer, I could see that she had our son in her arms, and, um, she was feeding him, and she was rocking him, and she was actually singing to him.
retellable.why: A personal origin story of KP's culture of compassion.

retellable.title: Hiring the medical groups' right hands
retellable.summary: Asked to strengthen the Federation, Grant asked to hire the medical groups' best people, and the medical directors agreed until they heard the names. The tension led to a design where leaders kept regional roles while serving nationally.
retellable.quote: when I started to name the individuals that I thought would be great in these roles, all of a sudden, I think one by one they realized that these are our right hands.
retellable.why: Shows how the Federation's distributed leadership model was born.

retellable.title: No day off from March to July
retellable.summary: During the pandemic Grant worked every day, including weekends, from early March through July 4th as KP planned to triple hospital capacity. He calls it exhausting but the most purposeful time, with turf wars set aside.
retellable.quote: it was also the most purposeful time because, um, nobody second guessed each other. There was, um, unbelievable alignment.
retellable.why: Captures how crisis aligned KP's parts around one goal.
